newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Hundreds mass at Sofia cathedral for rally.
newsitem.headline: Hundreds mass at Sofia cathedral for rally.

text.p: Hundreds of opposition supporters massed outside Sofia's gold-domed cathedral on Sunday, hours before the scheduled start of an opposition rally.
Riot police surrounded the presidency, where officials said they feared a repeat of the August 1990 burning of the Communist Party headquarters.
"We are determined not to allow anything to happen," said an official at the presidency, where police clashed with demonstrators on Saturday hours after breaking a siege of parliament.
The opposition called a rally for 4 p.m. (1400 GMT) at its traditional meeting point outside the Alexander Nevsky Cathedral.
Taking their cue from events in Yugoslavia, opposition leaders have vowed to stage daily countrywide protests until the discredited government agrees to hold a general election.
Protesters who returned to parliament to keep vigil on Saturday hours after being driven away by police with clubs, gathered with red, white and green Bulgarian flags and blue opposition flags.
Sofia university students, who have declared a strike in support of the opposition's demands, marched through the city centre.
The ruling Socialists on Sunday responded to President Zhelyu Zhelev's refusal to ask them to form a new government by ruling out early elections.
Bulgaria's Holy Synod ordered masses for peace to be said in Orthodox churches throughout the country on Sunday after 196 people were injured in clashes on Friday and Saturday.
